summary: This program counts upward one number at a time, pausing after each one to ask the user whether to continue, and stops only when the user types "stop". It shows a loop whose ending is decided by the person at the keyboard rather than by a fixed count.

lines.text: A condition that is always true means the loop never ends on its own; the only way out is the break inside the body. This is the shape you reach for when you cannot know in advance how many times the loop should run.

lines.code: s = input("Press Enter to continue or type stop: ")
lines.text: The loop pauses here on every pass, which is what lets the user, rather than a counter, decide when the program finishes. Pressing Enter alone hands back an empty string, which is not the stop word, so counting continues.

Calling strip removes stray spaces and the newline, and lower folds capitals down, so STOP and ' Stop ' are all accepted. Comparing raw input would reject anything but a perfectly typed lowercase word.
The break statement is the exit door out of an infinite loop; it abandons the loop immediately and continues with whatever follows it.
Because this sits after the break, it only runs when the user chose to continue, so the number shown next time is one higher.
